name: ThighMaster

card.summary: A spring-loaded V-shaped squeeze device marketed in 1990s infomercials to tone the inner thighs for a firmer leg shape.
card.note: Resistance is light; it works the hip adductors only.

quick.overview:
The ThighMaster is two metal tubes joined by a hinge and spring, squeezed between the knees to work the inner-thigh muscles (hip adductors). People use it to firm and shape the thighs as part of a leg-toning routine.

It became a 1990s fad through infomercials fronted by actress Suzanne Somers. It was designed originally as a physical therapy device, and no clinical trials of the product itself were found.
quick.how: Users squeeze the padded arms together between the thighs in repeated contractions, usually seated or lying down, and some adapt it for arms or chest. It is typically used alongside other exercise.
quick.risks: It is low-impact and widely considered low-risk. Users with joint or back problems are commonly advised to check with a healthcare professional before use. Muscle building by an inner-thigh squeeze does not target fat in that area; this is the general exercise-science position on spot reduction.

lead: The ThighMaster is a compact resistance exerciser made of two metal tubes bent into a loop and joined by a hinge. The user squeezes it between the knees to work the hip adductors of the inner thighs [1]. People use it to tone and firm the thighs, and the device can also be pressed between other body parts such as the arms [1].

It originated as a physical therapy tool called the V-Bar, credited to Anne Marie Bennstrom (Prescott) in Sweden, and received a US design patent as a physical exerciser. Joshua Reynolds marketed it as the ThighMaster and is often wrongly named as its inventor [1]. Suzanne Somers promoted it in 1990s infomercials, saying her company took over the V-Toner and renamed it ThighMaster [1].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports about 10 million units sold in the first few years at $19.95 and around 15 million overall; these figures are unverified [2]. No clinical studies of the ThighMaster itself were found.

angle.text: The device trains the inner-thigh adductors with light spring resistance, which proponents say firms the look of the thighs. It is used as an add-on to broader leg and body training.

paras: Two steel tubes with padded contact surfaces meet at a spring hinge; compressing the arms against the spring creates resistance [1][2]. Later versions added colors and adjustable tension [2].

The device began as the V-Bar, a therapy tool, and was later rebranded as the V-Toner before becoming ThighMaster [1][2]. Infomercials showed people exercising while watching TV [1]. It was referenced in 1990s television and is categorized among 1980s and 1990s fitness fads [1]. A companion product, the ButtMaster, followed [2].
The usual exercise is a seated or lying squeeze of the device between the knees, repeated in sets [2]. Grokipedia also describes arm and chest variations [2].
On T Nation the ThighMaster appears mainly as a joke about gym equipment, though one poster described using an adductor-style superset for weak abductors and glutes [3].

timeline.event: V-Bar developed as a physical therapy tool [2]
Rebranded and sold as ThighMaster through infomercials [2]
